name: Dipalmitoyl hydroxyproline (Sepilift DPHP)

card.summary: A lipoamino acid cosmetic ingredient sold by the supplier SEPPIC as Sepilift DPHP, added to creams and serums with the aim of improving the look of skin firmness and elasticity.
card.note: Published efficacy data are from the manufacturer's own study.

quick.overview:
Dipalmitoyl hydroxyproline is a cosmetic active made by combining the amino acid hydroxyproline with palmitic acid. It is marketed to formulators under the trade name Sepilift DPHP and appears in skin-care products positioned for firmness and elasticity.

Hydroxyproline is a major component of collagen, which is why it is used in anti-aging skin-care concepts. The supplier reported a 20-volunteer study in which a 1% use level reduced wrinkles versus placebo.
quick.how: It is an ingredient rather than a stand-alone product: it is added by cosmetic formulators to creams, serums and similar leave-on products applied to the face and neck.
quick.risks: Like other cosmetic ingredients, it can cause irritation or allergy in some individuals. No independent peer-reviewed safety or efficacy publications are known.

lead: Dipalmitoyl hydroxyproline (INCI name) is a lipoamino acid used in cosmetics and sold by SEPPIC under the name Sepilift DPHP. Personal Care Magazine describes it as a dipalmitoyl hydroxyproline lipovector, an anti-wrinkle ingredient that moisturises skin and reduces visible signs of ageing. [1]

The rationale is that hydroxyproline is a major component of collagen, so a lipid-linked form is positioned as a way to deliver it from topical products. [2] SEPPIC reported in 2007 a study of 20 volunteers in which a 1% use level reduced wrinkles by 32 percent compared with placebo and by 16 percent compared with a benchmark lipopeptide. [1]

chain: Applied in a cream or serum
Supplier says it carries hydroxyproline into skin
Skin looks firmer with fewer visible wrinkles
angle.text: Used as an ingredient in anti-aging skin care aimed at firmness and elasticity. The supporting data come from the ingredient's maker.

paras: The ingredient is a derivative of hydroxyproline carrying two palmitic acid chains, supplied to cosmetic manufacturers rather than sold to consumers directly. SEPPIC calls it a lipovector. [1]

Hydroxyproline is proline modified with a hydroxyl group after protein synthesis. It makes up roughly 13.5 percent of mammalian collagen and stabilises the collagen triple helix. It was isolated from gelatin by Hermann Emil Fischer in 1902. [2]

No studies found in independent peer-reviewed literature. SEPPIC's own in vivo study of 20 volunteers, announced in August 2007, compared a 1% use level with placebo and a benchmark lipopeptide and reported wrinkle reductions of 32 and 16 percent respectively; duration and measurement methods were not given. [1]

timeline.event: Hermann Emil Fischer isolates hydroxyproline from hydrolysed gelatin. [2]
SEPPIC announces an in vivo anti-ageing study of Sepilift DPHP in 20 volunteers. [1]
